questions.q: What makes science exciting according to Grade 6?
questions.a: It answers questions from everyday life - why things float, how magnets point, what food is made of.

questions.q: Give one question about your surroundings science can answer.
questions.a: Why does a compass needle always point north-south?

questions.q: What should a young scientist carry everywhere?
questions.a: Curiosity - the habit of asking 'why' about everything seen.

questions.q: List the steps of the scientific method.
questions.a: Observe, ask a question, guess (hypothesise), test with an experiment, record and conclude.

questions.q: Why is guessing (hypothesis) important in science?
questions.a: It gives a testable idea; the experiment then proves it right or wrong.
Honest recording of observations and a conclusion based on evidence.

concepts.title: Science in Everyday Life: The Bicycle

questions.q: Name two parts of a bicycle that show science at work.
questions.a: The chain and gears transfer your push to wheels; the air-filled tyres reduce bumps (cushioning).

questions.q: Why does a bicycle stop when brakes are pressed?
questions.a: Brake pads press the wheel; friction between them slows and stops the wheel.

questions.q: What simple machine does a bicycle pedal use?
questions.a: The pedal and crank work like a wheel-and-axle, multiplying your effort.

questions.q: Name any three topics you will study in Grade 6 science.
questions.a: Components of food, magnets, and measurement of length (also water cycle, separation).

questions.q: How do the topics of Grade 6 connect to daily life?
questions.a: Food, water, magnets, measurements - all appear around us every day.

questions.q: What is the best way to learn these topics?
questions.a: Try activities, observe closely, record results and discuss them.
